fixes.explanation: A wall, baker? Not this time. The text says Aaron built an altar before the calf (Exodus 32:5). Then he proclaimed, "Tomorrow shall be a feast to the LORD." The next day they offer burnt offerings and present peace offerings (Exodus 32:6).

Evil, baker, and Aaron says it like he's reading the blame off a cue card. Moses asks how the people could have led him into so great a sin (Exodus 32:21). Aaron's first move is to say, "Do not be enraged, my lord…" and then he points at the crowd: "You yourself know that the people are intent on evil." (Exodus 32:22) I think Aaron hopes that if everyone else is standing in the spotlight, nobody will look at him. Kevin Hart couldn't dodge a question that fast, and I've tried it myself.

problems.problem: It has 6 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.
It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.
Saying the altar was set up so offerings could be brought adds a purpose the passage does not state.
The explanation mechanically walks through the verses without much of Papa Dorin’s voice or insight.
